Learning Changes in Graphon Attachment Network Models
Xinyuan Fan 1 Bufan Li 1 Chenlei Leng 2 Weichi Wu 1
Abstract
This paper introduces Graphon Attachment Net-
work Models (GAN-M), a novel framework for
modeling evolving networks with rich structural
dependencies, grounded in graphon theory. GAN-
M provides a flexible and interpretable founda-
tion for studying network formation by leveraging
graphon functions to define attachment probabili-
ties, thereby combining the strengths of graphons
with a temporal perspective. A key contribution
of this work is a methodology for learning struc-
